forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: Combined Authority lacked risk management arrangements and approved Risk Management Policy in its first three months, with no performance monitoring produced
findings.detail: In its initial period of operation, the Authority did not have expected arrangements to manage operating and business risks. During the year under review, no performance information or financial performance reports were produced to monitor risks, and no approved Risk Management Policy was in place. The auditor identifies this as a significant weakness in governance and in improving economy, efficiency and effectiveness.
findings.matters: Without formal risk management and performance monitoring arrangements, the Authority cannot demonstrate it can navigate operating uncertainties, manage financial risks, or assure delivery of its strategic objectives.
findings.figures: First three months of operation; year under review
findings.quote: In the Combined Authority's first three months of operation, it did not have the expected arrangements in place to manage its operating and business risks. During the year under review, no performance information or financial performance reports were produced to monitor these risks. Additionally, the Authority lacked an approved Risk Management Policy that would have identified and mitigated weaknesses in performance delivery.

findings.headline: During 2024/25 the Audit and Governance Committee did not receive regular internal audit reports from Policing and Fire & Rescue functions
findings.detail: In-year internal audit updates from the Policing and Fire & Rescue functions were reported separately to the Joint Independent Audit Committee and Independent Audit Committee rather than to the main Audit and Governance Committee. This resulted in the main committee lacking full oversight and visibility of the Combined Authority's internal control environment across the full range of its responsibilities.
findings.matters: Those charged with governance could not obtain sufficient assurance over risk management, internal controls and financial reporting processes across the full authority, limiting their ability to approve financial statements and governance statements with complete information.
findings.figures: During 2024/25; reported to separate committees only
findings.quote: During 2024/25 the Audit and Governance Committee did not receive regular update reports from the Internal Audit function of the Policing and Fire & Rescue functions. As a result, the Audit and Governance Committee as those charged with governance for the Combined Authority, lacked oversight and visibility of the Combined Authority's internal control environment for 2024/25 across the full range of responsibility of the Combined Authority throughout the year.

findings.headline: Medium Term Financial Strategy absent; management stated it will not be prepared until late 2025 due to finance team capacity constraints
findings.detail: The Combined Authority has not developed an MTFS. Management indicated that capacity constraints within the finance team mean one will not be prepared until late 2025. The auditor identifies this absence as a significant weakness affecting both financial sustainability and governance, as an MTFS should enable the Authority to understand its financial outlook and identify potential savings gaps or funding issues.
findings.matters: Without a Medium Term Financial Strategy, the Authority cannot demonstrate it has identified unplanned savings or funding gaps that could substantially threaten the delivery of its financial plan.
findings.quote: Management has indicated that, due to capacity constraints within the finance team, it will not prepare and publish an MTFS until late 2025. An MTFS should support the financial sustainability of the Authority by enabling it to have a thorough understanding of its financial outlook and the associated impact on its ability to achieve its strategic objectives. Without an MTFS the Authority risks not being able to do this.

findings.headline: Draft financial statements for 2023/24 published 16 January 2025, missing the statutory 31 May 2024 deadline, with casting and consistency errors identified
findings.detail: The Combined Authority's initial draft statements were published eight months late. The auditor's review identified quality control issues in the accounts production process, including casting and consistency errors. The auditor attributes these issues to the finance team's lack of capacity and capability.
findings.matters: Repeated delays in statutory accounts publication and quality control failures signal underlying financial management and capacity issues that affect the reliability of financial reporting.
findings.figures: Published 16 January 2025 vs statutory deadline 31 May 2024
findings.quote: For the period ending 31 March 2024, the draft financial statements were published on 16 January 2025, missing the statutory 31 May 2024 deadline. In addition to this delay, our initial review of the draft financial statements identified issues with the quality control process supporting the production of the accounts, including casting and consistency errors.

findings.headline: Mayoral Investment Fund programmes reprioritised with net reduction of £0.443m over MTFP; shift from capital to revenue delivery reflects updated delivery forecasts.
findings.detail: Review of the MIF portfolio concluded additional revenue funding is required for programme delivery while several capital allocations are no longer required at previous levels. MIF Revenue Programme budget increased by £1.182m and Capital Programme reduced by £1.625m in 2026/27. Changes affect Skills Innovation Fund, Active Travel, Town Centres & High Streets and Cost of Living initiatives.
findings.matters: Significant mid-year reprioritisation of delivery approach suggests previous capital intensity assumptions were incorrect, indicating either market changes in how programmes can be delivered or delivery challenges with capital-heavy approaches.
findings.figures: Net reduction £0.443m over MTFP; 2026/27: revenue increase £1.225m, capital decrease £1.837m
findings.quote: The review has concluded that additional revenue funding is required to support programme delivery, whilst several capital allocations are no longer required at the levels previously assumed.
